summary: Rabbi Tawil begins the second half of the book of Yehoshua, which focuses on the process of settling the land of Eretz Yisrael after the initial conquests. He examines the list of 31 Canaanite kings in chapter 12, explaining the rabbinic tradition regarding how such lists are structured on parchment compared to other sections of the Tanakh.
questions: Why did it take longer to settle the land than to conquer it?
How does the structure of the list of 31 kings compare to other parts of the Tanakh?
What is the connection between Moshe Rabbenu's conquests and Yehoshua's?
Why are some Canaanite nations mentioned while others are not?
